page: Microsoft Azure DC48eds_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine based on an Intel processor platform and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of memory, resulting in an even 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per core. It does not include hardware acceleration, with zero GPUs present in the specification.

Storage architecture is characterized by 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity integrated directly with the instance, alongside support for Premium Storage volumes. This bundled solid-state configuration offers low-latency transient disk space directly on the host node without reliance on network-attached storage for temporary caching. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

With its 48 dedicated execution threads and expansive local solid-state footprint, the DC48eds_v6 delivers dense compute and scratch storage capabilities. The balanced ratio of processing cores to memory makes it structurally suited for relational databases, big data analytics, ETL processing routines, and demanding enterprise application hosting environments.
description: Microsoft Azure DC48eds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated x86_64 Intel vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes 2835 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations, catering to I/O-intensive temporary data operations. There are no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses allocated to the system. With its high vCPU count and substantial attached solid-state storage, the instance delivers resource density that reduces the need for external caching volumes. The hardware profile is well structured for transactional databases, large-scale web application serving, ETL processing pipelines, and data analytics tasks requiring sustained multi-core processing alongside high-capacity local disk performance.
